text: The Patriots' dominant 20-3 victory over the Pittsburgh Steelers at home came with a significant price tag: starting right guard Mike Onwenu suffered a broken right ankle that will require further evaluation, casting a shadow over an otherwise impressive defensive performance that allowed the team to win despite what analysts describe as a continued lack of offensive rhythm from last season's Super Bowl run. TreVeyon Henderson found the end zone as the Patriots' ground game provided the offensive punch, though the overall unit has yet to recapture the form that carried them through their championship campaign, leaving head coach Mike Vrabel and company to grapple with both the injury to their interior offensive line and the broader offensive inconsistency even as the defense proved it can carry games. The win marked a historic milestone for the franchise, as New England became the first of the original AFL teams to reach 600 victories, a testament to sustained excellence across decades—though the immediate concern now shifts to how the team will manage life without Onwenu's services going forward.
